races.name: Think Print & Design Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Plastic Paddy
runners_data.note: Veteran of 8 with a consistent pattern of finishing positions suggesting a hold-up style — recent form of PPP indicates he has been pulled up in his last three starts, and at 166lbs and 15 days since last run, the fitness angle is questionable; he will race further back than his mapped midfield position suggests.

runners_data.name: Sea Eagle
runners_data.note: Thomas O'Connor (7lb claimer) takes the ride for Gerard O'Leary whose stable had one winner from 14 runners in the past fortnight — genuine hold-up type placed further forward on the map than his natural style warrants, with his best recent effort a second over 2m2f on Good the most relevant piece of form here.

runners_data.name: Storm Eric
runners_data.note: Keith Donoghue partners this Jamie Flynn-trained 7-year-old who has an excellent record of placing at Dundalk on the all-weather (five consecutive top-4 finishes) but has had 133 days off and now switches to turf on Good ground for the first time — the style and jumping credentials are unknown quantities on this surface.

runners_data.name: Earthwatch
runners_data.note: Denis Gerard Hogan's four-year-old has been consistent in fourth across a variety of trips and going, and suits this distance profile on Good ground given 13 of 14 qualifying runs were in similar conditions — though his natural closer's instinct will be squeezed by the crowded rear of the field, he is one of the better-credentialed horses in the race.

runners_data.name: Champagne Diamond
runners_data.note: 368 days off the track is the standout concern here — this TJ O'Mara-trained 6-year-old arrives completely cold, with only one run in comparable Good-ground conditions and a form string suggesting he has never threatened to win; the fade-in-finish flag compounds an already uncertain fitness picture.

runners_data.name: Drumconnor Hill
runners_data.note: Cian Collins sends this 5-year-old out 15 days after his last run, with three runs on Good ground all ending in mid-division finishes; his true hold-up style will be difficult to execute in such a large field, and his best recent efforts over 2m and 2m4f suggest the trip is not a limiting factor.

runners_data.name: Kingston Silver
runners_data.note: Danny Mullins takes the ride for WJ Lanigan, whose stable has returned 0 wins from 4 runners in the past fortnight — going and style are both unknown, making this lightly-raced 5-year-old one of the most opaque runners in the race; Mullins' tactical acumen may be crucial if this horse has ability.

runners_data.name: Langage Du Large
runners_data.note: Ian Power partners this PJ Breen-trained 5-year-old who has not run for 453 days and whose only hurdles form includes a fall — the extended absence and absence of a clear style make this one of the most speculative entries in the race, with the unknown going preference a further complication.

runners_data.name: Penny Express
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's 6-year-old ridden by Jack Kennedy is a confirmed front-runner on Good ground, placing in nine of eleven runs in similar conditions — 15 days since last run suggests freshness, and Kennedy will ensure she gets to the front; she is the more likely of the two front-runners to control terms given trainer quality and jockey profile.

runners_data.name: Rosenborg
runners_data.note: PJ Rothwell's 5-year-old under Mr R Sugrue (7lb claimer) is the second confirmed front-runner, and with a best recent effort of second over 2m2f on Good, has the class to compete — the amateur rider and trainer's current strike rate of 0 from 18 over 14 days introduces a degree of caution about the stability of his early pace-setting.

runners_data.name: Sum Story
runners_data.note: PJ Rothwell sends out this 5-year-old 54 days after its last run, with a single comparable run on Good ground ending tenth — the fade-in-finish flag and limited form make this a hard one to assess, and his natural hold-up style in such a large field will make position-finding difficult.

runners_data.name: Tell Me See
runners_data.note: Eoin Walsh partners this John M Burke-trained 5-year-old who has finished 8th and 9th in both career hurdles starts on Good ground — the fade-in-finish flag aligns with the form, and while 14 days since last run is acceptable, there is little in the record to suggest a competitive effort at this level.

runners_data.name: Tomthescaffolder
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead's 6-year-old ridden by Darragh O'Keeffe has form figures of 3-4-4-6-4 over distances and going very close to today's conditions, and the trainer's T14 return of 4/31 is the strongest of any yard in the race — a hold-up horse who can realistically secure a prominent midfield position in a well-run race, he looks a principal player.

runners_data.name: Run For Power
runners_data.note: C Byrnes' 6-year-old returns after 306 days off the track with limited hurdles form — both runs on Good ground ended fourth and twelfth, and the extended layoff combined with his natural tendency to race from further back than his mapped position suggests make this an uncertain proposition at a competitive price.

runners_data.name: You Lift Me Up
runners_data.note: PJ Rothwell's 4-year-old has not had a jockey listed and has only one run to reference — an 11th on Good ground 22 days ago; the fade-in-finish flag and the trainer's low recent strike rate combine to make this one of the least compelling runners in the field.

runners_data.name: Ribadora
runners_data.note: Eoin Christopher McCarthy's 4-year-old has three runs on Good ground, finishing 5th, 7th, and 13th, and 73 days since last run is a moderate gap — at 148lbs, the lowest weight in the race offers some assistance, but a genuine hold-up runner in a field packed with similar types means clean air will be at a premium throughout.

races.paceDynamic: Penny Express (Jack Kennedy, Gordon Elliott) and Rosenborg (Mr R Sugrue) are the two confirmed front-runners in a 16-horse maiden hurdle on Good ground at Wexford, and with both likely to press forward from the jump, this race will be run at an honest, competitive gallop from the outset with no opportunity for either to dictate on their own terms. The contested lead will ensure a genuine tempo through the early and middle stages, which on Good ground over 2m1f typically sets up a strongly-run race that plays into the hands of horses who can settle in behind and travel with cover before producing their effort from the home turn. Closers and prominent racers with a strong late jump will be best placed, while true front-runners who expend energy fighting for position risk emptying before the final hurdle. The field holds considerably more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear — Sea Eagle, Run For Power, Ribadora, Plastic Paddy, Drumconnor Hill, and Earthwatch are all genuine hold-up horses redistributed to midfield, meaning Tomthescaffolder, Storm Eric, and Tell Me See are those most likely to actually secure the prominent-to-midfield berths they need; in a race this congested, the horses best served will be those who can find a natural rhythm in the first-half-dozen without burning fuel fighting for position.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead, Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Penny Express and Rosenborg fight for the early lead and set a genuine pace that strings the field out, draining the front two before the last.
scenarios.body: The honest gallop produced by two front-runners battling for supremacy will leave the pace-setters vulnerable in the closing stages, gifting a winning opportunity to horses who settled in behind and have an engine left from the home turn onward.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Runner Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If one of the hold-up horses redistributed to midfield manages to find a prominent position early and travels fluidly in the first few, they steal a march on the true closers.
scenarios.body: With the field strung out behind two front-runners, a horse travelling prominently with something in reserve can kick before the final hurdle and hold on as the hold-up types fail to close from deeper; Tomthescaffolder and Penny Express both fit this profile if the pace moderates slightly.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If one of Penny Express or Rosenborg secures an uncontested or lightly-pressed lead and the other fades quickly, allowing one to dictate at a comfortable gallop.
scenarios.body: A solo front-runner setting their own tempo on Good ground can conserve enough energy to jump the final hurdle and sprint clear; Jack Kennedy's tactical intelligence on Penny Express makes this the more credible of the two front-runners to exploit it.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Scrappy Pace, Bunched Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the two front-runners cancel each other out early and the pace collapses to a crawl, turning this into a sprint from the home turn.
scenarios.body: A messy, slow-run race with a bunch finish randomises the outcome and can produce a winner from almost anywhere in the field, with horses who jump well at the final two flights gaining a significant advantage regardless of running style.

watchPoints.text: Watch Penny Express and Rosenborg at the start — if both stride forward aggressively in the first two furlongs, the contested pace will be genuine enough to set up a closers' race and fundamentally shift the likely winner away from either front-runner.

Tomthescaffolder (Darragh O'Keeffe, De Bromhead T14: 4/31) is the standout in-form yard runner and should be tracked from the home turn — if he travels fluently in midfield through the early stages, his consistent placing record makes him a key danger.

Kingston Silver (Danny Mullins) has an experienced jockey on a completely unexposed 5-year-old with unknown going and style — in a wide-open maiden hurdle, unknown quantities ridden by top pilots can surprise; watch his early positioning.

With six horses genuinely redistributed from the rear of the field, the early stages are likely to be physically congested — watch for any horses who get shuffled back further than intended or are denied a clean passage, as this could neutralise the chances of Sea Eagle, Earthwatch, Ribadora, and Run For Power entirely.

Storm Eric has an impeccable Dundalk placing record but has not run for 133 days and switches to turf — watch his jumping in the early stages as a novice hurdler making a surface switch; a clean round under Keith Donoghue could see him figure, but a jumping error could end his race early.

races.name: Treo Eile Mares Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Chosen Shant
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer who has won and placed multiple times on Good, ran 1st and 2nd in last two on identical going — 16 days fresh, headgear worn, Phillip Enright positive booking; sits best positioned to stalk Annarubyrose throughout.
runners_data.comment: Chosen Shant arrives on the back of a second last time out and a winner two starts back, boasting experience over today's trip and going; carrying 168 lb is the one query, but she heads this 17-runner field as the clear form pick.

runners_data.name: Eaglewood
runners_data.note: Prominent type for Leonard Paul Flynn, handles Good going well (9/10 sim-going appearances), but recent form shows a string of disappointing runs including last in most recent outing — needs a significant bounce back.
runners_data.comment: Eaglewood shaped with promise when third two starts back, and she has run over today's trip and going before at a testing 165 lb; the concern is she has been winless in her last five starts, and her unplaced effort since that third needs improvement.

runners_data.name: Tropical Twist
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy rides this hold-up mare for Gordon Elliott — placed in two of her last four but has a fall and pulled-up on her card; true hold-up style suits a stronger pace scenario and Kennedy's strength will be needed late.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, with a pull-up and a fall among recent outings, Tropical Twist carries a hefty 163 lb and has a trainer badly out of form at 1/44 over the past fortnight; she has run over today's trip and going before, but there is plenty working against her here.

runners_data.name: Teagarden Jazz
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up operator who has been off 83 days and returns on a going surface she has found difficult historically (13/15 in sim-going); tongue-tie worn, amateur jockey, short of realistic winning prospects here.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts and pulling up two back is a concern, but she has experience over today's trip and going, and a rating of 105 ranks her second of 17 — the main risk is reproducing that pulled-up effort under 161 lb after 83 days off.

runners_data.name: Backwithyourown
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with a decent second on Good in her last five, but recent form reads U/0 at the business end; handles Good ground but finishing efforts have been patchy and she hasn't won from this style recently.
runners_data.comment: Backwithyourown arrives here 28 days fresh, with experience of today's distance and going working in her favour, but she's winless in her last five starts and that unseating incident lurks in the recent record; a second four starts back offers some encouragement, though 160 lb is a stern ask.

runners_data.name: Annarubyrose
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner — Josh Williamson (5) rides this five-year-old who handles Good ground (8/8 sim-going), placed twice at this level; controls the race shape entirely and her willingness to bowl along unchallenged is the key tactical factor for the whole field.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Annarubyrose does hold a second three starts back to her name, though fifth and fourth in more recent outings suggest she's knocking without quite breaking through; experience over today's trip and going at least removes those unknowns under 159 lb.

runners_data.name: Tudorista
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare dropping into the field for Edward Power, has a tongue-tie on, and has finished no better than fourth in any of her last six; mapped to midfield despite hold-up tendency — 14 days between runs, nothing in the form to flag.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and pulled up most recently, Tudorista faces an uphill task off 157 lb, though she has run over today's distance and going before and a return to form isn't impossible at a rating of 90.

runners_data.name: Tellmemamema
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who has shown progressive placing at 20f on Good, regularly hitting the frame in those distances — but distances here are slightly shorter than her best and she will struggle to get a clear run from a crowded midfield position.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Tellmemamema has been going the wrong way with fifth two starts back and fourth three starts back, and has run over today's trip and going; the 152 lb burden is a stiff ask for a mare yet to find the winner's enclosure.

runners_data.name: Erne Star
runners_data.note: Returns from a 955-day absence — extraordinary layoff — for Francis Casey; hold-up racer pushed into midfield in this shape, fades in finish tag, and sim-going record of just 1/4 suggests this is likely a reappearance run only.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts and absent for over 950 days, Erne Star faces a stiff task on return, ranked 13th of 17 on our figures; has run over today's trip, but the lengthy layoff makes her hard to fancy here.

runners_data.name: Lady Victrix
runners_data.note: Paul Flynn's hold-up mare is naturally a rear-of-field type but will be shuffled closer than ideal in this race shape; the style-fit discount is real — her best form comes from tracking pace that doesn't exist here, and a 15-day turnaround is short.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, with a pulled up and two unplaced efforts among recent outings, Lady Victrix cuts a difficult profile — ranked 15 of 17 on our figures, carrying 147 lb, and with a trainer hitting just 5% over the past fortnight, there is little obvious encouragement despite going experience.

runners_data.name: Wings Of Africa
runners_data.note: Hold-up fiver from W J Lanigan who has placed at 6th at this distance on Good — will be forced closer than her natural position and her fades-in-finish tag reinforces that she is unlikely to hit the frame unless the pace truly falls apart.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, with two pulls-up among them, Wings Of Africa faces a stiff task carrying 145 lb and ranked near the foot of our figures; familiarity with today's going is slim consolation for a mare in such ragged form.

runners_data.name: Stormy Jenn
runners_data.note: Veteran nine-year-old hold-up mare, has placed third at 16f on Heavy in the past, but a fades-in-finish pattern and being pushed out of her natural rearward slot by the volume of hold-up types makes a bold show very unlikely.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked 12 of 17 on our figures, Stormy Jenn's recent profile — unplaced, a fall, and a pull-up — makes her hard to fancy, though she has run over today's trip and going, and a third four starts back offers a faint glimmer.

runners_data.name: Avandra
runners_data.note: Shane O'Callaghan (3) rides this P J Rothwell mare who has two places at 16f on Good and wears a tongue-tie and blinkers — hold-up style is genuine but she is one of the more capable of this group on form and could be the best of the redistributed closers if the pace collapses.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked 14th of 17 on our figures, Avandra faces a stiff task, with a trainer in the depths of a lean spell (1 from 26 in the last fortnight); she has run over today's trip and going before, but that's faint consolation here.

runners_data.name: La Rocca Lass
runners_data.note: 109 days between runs, fades-in-finish flag, tongue-tie, and a form line reading 90000 — a hold-up type who has been well beaten in all her recent starts and faces a steep ask on return from a layoff in a competitive field.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and absent for 109 days, La Rocca Lass arrives short of recent encouragement, though she has run over today's distance and going before and a rating of 89 suggests some unexposed ability worth respecting.

runners_data.name: Maxios Lady
runners_data.note: 315 days absent, no jockey listed, hold-up style forced into midfield here, fades-in-finish note, and a form line of 000P — this is almost certainly a fitness run for P J Rothwell and not a realistic winning contender.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts and pulled up most recently, Maxios Lady returns after a 315-day absence for a yard firing at just 4% — she has plenty to prove before asking for confidence here.

runners_data.name: Game Phoenix
runners_data.note: Paul Power-trained hold-up type who is OR 97 — the highest rated in the field — with four career places on Good, though recent runs show 7th and 9th; the step back up in trip from 10f to 16f is positive and she represents the biggest slide off a lofty mark if things fall right.

runners_data.name: Annie Agnew
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for Gerald Quinn with a win and three places on Good at these distances — 77 days off but has shown she stays the trip well; headgear note (hg:p), and her record suggests she is a natural stalk-and-pounce type who suits the dominant scenario.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Annie Agnew nevertheless brings distance and going experience to the table, and our rating of 104 marks her out as a leading threat in a 17-runner field. Carrying 165 lb is the concern.

races.paceDynamic: Annarubyrose is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 17-runner field and, with no genuine challenger disputing the lead, she should be able to dictate her own comfortable gallop from the front on Good ground at Wexford. Chosen Shant, Eaglewood, Backwithyourown, and Annie Agnew will push forward from their prominent styles to sit just off her, meaning the early sections will be reasonably honest but not brutal — a measured, controlled pace rather than a true test of stamina. This field holds significantly more hold-up types than can realistically settle at the rear; Lady Victrix, Erne Star, Wings Of Africa, Stormy Jenn, Avandra, La Rocca Lass, and Maxiles Lady are all genuine hold-up operators but will be forced closer to the pace than they want, making them unreliable closers in this shape. A single-paced, uncontested lead at an honest but not extreme gallop on Good ground at Wexford favours organised, prominent racers who can travel just behind the pace and pick off a tiring leader in the straight — hold-up horses forced wide and closer than ideal are structurally disadvantaged.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Annarubyrose Controls, Prominent Striker
scenarios.trigger: If Annarubyrose gets a clean lead and dictates a fair but measured pace unchallenged into the straight.
scenarios.body: Annarubyrose sets the fractions she wants and the prominent horses behind her travel comfortably, with the winner coming from just off the pace in the final two flights where the leader is caught on the run-in.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Late Rush
scenarios.trigger: If Annarubyrose goes too slow and the race turns into a sprint-finish, allowing the freshest legs to close.
scenarios.body: A falsely-run race compresses the field and the straight becomes a dash, favouring horses with tactical speed who find room late; the congested midfield creates scrimmaging.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Go Too Fast
scenarios.trigger: If the cluster of prominent types — Chosen Shant, Eaglewood, Annie Agnew — push into Annarubyrose and force a stronger gallop than she wants.
scenarios.body: Annarubyrose is pressed into a contested pace and the race becomes a proper staying test, draining the prominent runners and opening the door for a genuine hold-up performer who finds a clear run.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Capitalises Fully
scenarios.trigger: If Annarubyrose gets so far clear on a very compressed field that she simply stays on unchallenged to the line.
scenarios.body: Annarubyrose uses her uncontested lead to conserve energy through the race and simply outstays all challengers in the straight on the Good going she handles well.

watchPoints.text: Annarubyrose controls every meaningful variable in this race — if Josh Williamson gets a clean break and settles into a rhythm unchallenged, the race shape is entirely set to her advantage and the outcome of all four scenarios flows from whether she is pressured or not.

Chosen Shant's form on Good going is outstanding (3W5P in 15 sim-going runs) and Phillip Enright rode a winner last time out — watch for him to track Annarubyrose through the race and challenge approaching the last; the most dangerous confirmed rival in the dominant shape.

Game Phoenix carries the top OR (97) but has been off 70 days, is a genuine hold-up type, and is racing further than her recent efforts — if she gets a clear run in the straight she could represent the biggest price upset in the race.

The cluster of Eaglewood, Backwithyourown, and Annie Agnew all pushing forward creates a minor danger that Annarubyrose gets bumped or shuffled early — watch the opening two furlongs for any incident that disrupts the settled lead.

Erne Star returns from 955 days off — watch for significant market drifting before the off and note her position in running purely as a fitness indicator for connections rather than a genuine form pointer.

races.name: Neville Hotels Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Jabbar
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with Gerard O'Leary form and a 7-year-old who handles Good well; returns off just 11 days with his best run on this going a seventh — will need a proper test to reel in the leaders.|
runners_data.comment: Jabbar arrives here on the back of a consistent run of form — a winner one start back, then placed second and third in succession before a fourth last time out, and he has experience of today's distance and going. The 11-day turnaround looks sharp enough, and his 133 rating marks him as the one to beat under 166 lb.

runners_data.name: Mode Avion
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's 4-year-old is the sole front-runner here and will get an uncontested lead, but the STYLE_FIT flag reflects that prominent/lead is not its settled role; thin sim-going record and a pull-up on latest start temper confidence.|
runners_data.comment: Mode Avion boasts a second and a win in his last five starts, has run over today's trip, and a rating of 130 sees him rank second of eight — a genuine threat. The concern is his trainer's dire recent form at 1/44, and he returns after 101 days off.

runners_data.name: Tassarolo
runners_data.note: Denis Hogan handler in good 14-day form (2/32); hold-up type on Good ground who returns 18 days after a seventh at Wexford — has one win on this surface but consistency has been elusive and will need the pace to quicken.|
runners_data.comment: Tassarolo brings a lively recent profile — a winner two starts back and a winner four starts back, with a second three starts back too — and he handles today's distance and going, making him a genuine threat; the key risk is bouncing back from an unplaced effort last time.

runners_data.name: Ma Belle Etoile
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead's 7-year-old has a 2W3P record on Good and sits naturally prominent; Darragh O'Keeffe is a major positive, and her fourth last time out followed a fall — she arrives fresh enough to strike here.|
runners_data.comment: Fell on her latest start is the obvious concern, but she showed real ability when winning three starts back, and has run over today's trip and going before. Carrying 154 lb is a stiff ask, though her rating of 119 suggests she retains solid claims if she bounces back.

runners_data.name: Shaboozee
runners_data.note: J J Slevin takes the mount on Joseph O'Brien's 5-year-old returning from 316 days off; the two wins and a second on Good ground are compelling, but the lengthy layoff is the dominant risk factor in an otherwise strong profile.|
runners_data.comment: Shaboozee won twice in his last five starts, and has run over today's trip and going, giving him solid claims here; the concern is a 316-day absence, which makes his return to action the one question mark over his participation.

runners_data.name: Now So Jake
runners_data.note: Genuine front-runner by nature but the crowded prominent contingent means Sean Flanagan will likely be forced to settle further back than ideal — a 736-day absence is the other major concern, and the STYLE_FIT flag applies.|
runners_data.comment: A 736-day absence makes Now So Jake enormously difficult to assess, and ranked seventh of eight on our figures the task of recommending him is harder still. Three wins in his last five starts and going experience offer faint encouragement, but the layoff is the overwhelming concern.

runners_data.name: Splashing Out
runners_data.note: Peter Smithers (7lb claimer) rides a true hold-up type back after just 9 days; the blinkers are noted, and while Splashing Out has won on Good ground, the redistribution reflects he is in his natural rear position — late runs at Wexford depend on the pace genuinely hotting up.|
runners_data.comment: Bounced back to win two starts back before flopping last time out, and she has run over today's trip and going before; the 150 lb burden is a stern ask, however, and her recent form is inconsistent.

runners_data.name: Wonderfulwonderful
runners_data.note: Alex Harvey rides the youngest horse in the field; a natural front-runner who will find himself tracking midfield against his instincts due to prominent congestion — the pace headgear, his short 9-day turnaround, and poor recent form (145-0) all weigh against.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of eight on our figures and representing a trainer without a winner in 31 attempts over the past fortnight, Wonderfulwonderful is hard to fancy despite her recent win four starts back; unplaced last time out and shouldering 148 lb, experience over today's trip and going is about all she offers here.

races.paceDynamic: Mode Avion is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with just one horse committed to leading, will dictate an honest but uncontested gallop around Wexford's flat, right-handed circuit. Ma Belle Etoile and Shaboozee are the natural prominent horses most likely to sit directly behind Mode Avion and keep tabs on the pace, while Now So Jake and Wonderfulwonderful — both genuine prominent types — are pushed into a midfield role by the congestion ahead of them and are unlikely to reproduce their natural racing position. With a single pace-setter setting a sustainable tempo over Good ground, this race shape strongly favours horses who can travel prominently or just off the pace and pounce from the second-last hurdle — hold-up horses like Jabbar, Tassarolo, and Splashing Out will need an acceleration to materialise late that the even pace may not generate. The field carries more front-running and prominent types than the map can accommodate cleanly, and it is Mode Avion, Ma Belle Etoile, and Shaboozee who are best placed to actually secure those forward positions.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prompt pace, prominent types land
scenarios.trigger: If Mode Avion leads at a sustainable clip and Ma Belle Etoile or Shaboozee travel prominently to pounce from the second-last.
scenarios.body: Mode Avion sets a metronomic Good-ground gallop and the race develops into a straight kick from two out, exactly suiting horses who have been travelling in the first three throughout. Ma Belle Etoile's 2W3P record on Good and Shaboozee's big-field winning form at similar distances make them the primary beneficiaries of this shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers get late run
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to string the field out and create a genuine test for those up front.
scenarios.body: Jabbar and Tassarolo, both hold-up types comfortable on Good ground, could sweep through if the prominent horses use each other up over the final mile. However, the lone front-runner scenario makes a truly gruelling pace unlikely, so this requires a specific burn-up between the prominent horses that is against the grain of this race shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-runner steals it
scenarios.trigger: If Mode Avion bowls along uncontested, conserves energy perfectly, and the chasing pack fails to close.
scenarios.body: With no pressure on Mode Avion through the early stages, Gordon Elliott's four-year-old could simply coast into a lead that is never seriously threatened — its sim-going record (1/7, 0W0P) is thin but its hurdling profile and style suit an uncontested lead on Good ground. This shape is discounted modestly because Mode Avion is noted as racing out of role and its recent form includes a fifth and a pull-up.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos — pace breaks up field
scenarios.trigger: If Now So Jake or Wonderfulwonderful push aggressively to find their natural prominent berth, injecting an unplanned surge.
scenarios.body: Both horses are true prominent types compressed into midfield, and if either attempts to assert, the pace could fragment, turning it into a more tactical scramble than the baseline shape suggests. This benefits riders who react fastest, but the scenario depends on horses racing well outside their mapped position, making it a low-probability outcome.

watchPoints.text: Shaboozee's 316-day absence is the key watch — if J J Slevin reports he moves freely in the early stages, the horse's two Good-ground wins suggest his fitness is intact and he becomes a serious danger.

Ma Belle Etoile fell last time and Darragh O'Keeffe may be instructed to settle her early — watch whether she finds her natural prominent pitch comfortably or gets into a battle for position with Shaboozee.

Now So Jake hasn't run in over two years (736 days) — monitor at the start and through the first two flights for any sign of ring-rustiness that could compromise Sean Flanagan's ability to find a prominent spot.
Mode Avion is the lone pace-setter: if it fails to jump off quickly or is challenged unexpectedly in the first half-mile, the entire race shape collapses and closer scenarios jump in probability.

Good ground has held all day at Wexford and is confirmed for this race — no going-related concerns apply, but the flat track rewards a well-timed jump at the last; watch for horses who are fluent over the final two hurdles.

races.name: SIS Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Mister Vic
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up performer who has the all-important good-ground form (sim-going 10/14, 1W3P) and won over 22f at this course configuration; the ⚠ fade flag is a concern over 3 miles if he needs to make sustained ground, but if he settles well behind a strong pace his best form gives him a chance; 63-day break needs noting.|
runners_data.comment: Landed a winner four starts back but has been unplaced in his two most recent outings, and 63 days off the track adds a fitness query; he has run over today's trip and going, though 168 lb is a stern ask.

runners_data.name: Charlie's Dilemma
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for John McConnell who was placed five times in 15 good-ground runs (0W5P); consistent rather than spectacular, and the step up to 3 miles is a question over 2m-2m4f form, but he's 15d fresh and the trainer has runners firing (T14: 0/25).|
runners_data.comment: Charlie's Dilemma has experience of today's trip and going, and our rating of 107 just edges him ahead of his 16 rivals, but he's winless in his last five starts and comes from a yard without a winner in 14 days.

runners_data.name: Clone Cross
runners_data.note: Five-year-old prominent racer with solid placed form at 24f on good ground (0W3P from sim-going); the form string contains falls and pulled-up runs so soundness must be queried, but he was second over 24f just 14 days ago and arrives in good nick for Cavanagh.|
runners_data.comment: Placed second last time out and third three starts back, Clone Cross has shown ability without a win in his last six starts, and his experience over today's trip and going is a clear asset; the main concern is a jumping record that includes a fall and two pull-ups in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Matter Of Opinion
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare who has raced consistently without landing a blow (0W2P from sim-going); headgear (tongue-pin) suggests some quirk, and the step from 20f to 24f over hurdles on this evidence hasn't unlocked improvement — hard to make a case at 3 miles.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and pulled up five runs back, Matter Of Opinion does at least bring distance and going experience to the table, and his rating of 102 suggests hidden ability — the concern is that recent form offers little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Gerrys Wish
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy takes the ride on a five-year-old with outstanding good-ground placed form (0W4P from 11/12 sim-going runs); twice placed at 24f on good ground and ran second here over the same course 15 days ago — the trip, going and jockey all align, and he's the archetypal horse to be produced late off a strong gallop.|
runners_data.comment: Gerrys Wish has been second three times in her last five starts but that pulled-up run lurks in the record, she's yet to win in recent form, and a trainer striking at just 2% is a concern; the trip and going hold no fears, though 161 lb is a stiff ask.

runners_data.name: Tango Theatre
runners_data.note: One of the two confirmed pace-setters; an 11-year-old who won over 26f on good ground (1W5P) and is well exposed but keeps honest; the concern is whether he has enough in reserve at this age if Mobile Mamma makes it a proper contest — a 26-day break should leave him fresh.|
runners_data.comment: Tango Theatre showed she can win in recent starts, and has run over today's trip and going, but four runs without a win since that victory are hard to ignore, and a trainer without a winner in 31 recent attempts is a significant concern under a hefty 160 lb.

runners_data.name: Glendine Billy
runners_data.note: Hold-up type for Danny Mullins with very modest recent form (0W2P, best finishes 8th and 9th); the drop back to 24f from longer trips hasn't helped him, and his history at this trip is uninspiring — needs the race to fall apart completely.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts, including a pull-up, Glendine Billy brings distance-and-going experience but is up against it from 156 lb; our rating of 96 suggests more ability than recent efforts show, yet the form line gives little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Mobile Mamma
runners_data.note: The other confirmed front-runner, a mare who won over 24f on good ground and was second at 23f last time (1W3P); she maps as a genuine leader and if she dictates her own race against an ageing Tango Theatre she is the most dangerous of the front two.|
runners_data.comment: Consistent mare who was second last time out and a winner four starts back, and she has run over today's trip and going before; 156 lb is a stern ask, however, and ranked ninth of seventeen she faces a stiff task against stronger rivals.

runners_data.name: Joe's Turn
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse by record (2W4P on good ground, including a win at 25f) who is pushed forward on the map due to the surfeit of hold-up types; racing out of role matters here — if he cannot get back to his natural position this 10-year-old's finishing kick will be compromised, and a 26-day break adds uncertainty.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts — including a fall in that sequence — Joe's Turn has run over today's trip and going before, yet a sixth and eighth in more recent outings give little encouragement; the 154 lb burden won't help his cause either.

runners_data.name: Set The Tone
runners_data.note: Won at 24f on good ground and placed at 22f (1W3P) so the form is there — a true hold-up racer who will be squeezed forward by the volume of hold-up horses in this field; his best form comes when he can creep into the race late, and he may struggle to replicate that here.|
runners_data.comment: Set The Tone has the form to catch the eye — a winner last time and second two starts back — but she's ranked 12th of 17 on our figures, and the pulled-up run three starts back is hard to ignore; 150 lb is a stern ask against this field.

runners_data.name: Fervida
runners_data.note: Poor recent form (0W0P from good-ground runs) with a ⚠ fade flag and a pattern of pulling up; a genuine hold-up horse who will be displaced from her natural berth, and there is very little in the record to suggest she can threaten even if she does get the right trip.|
runners_data.comment: Fervida has shown precious little in recent starts — unseating last time out after a pulled up and two ninths in her last five — yet she remains unexposed enough that improvement cannot be ruled out entirely, and 149 lb is a stern ask for a mare still finding her feet.

runners_data.name: Strong Contender
runners_data.note: Five-year-old with modest form figures at this trip (0W1P, best 7th in 5 good-ground runs); carries the ⚠ fade flag and has never won a hurdle — a 17-runner 3-mile handicap off a strong pace is a tough ask, and racing forward of his natural position reduces his chance further.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts — including a fall and two unplaced efforts — Strong Contender finds little encouragement in her recent form, and ranked 14th of 17 on our figures she faces a stiff task here, though she has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Clever Court
runners_data.note: Won at 20f on good ground (1W1P) and has shown ability when fresh; his true hold-up profile suits a strong-pace race in theory but the redistribution away from his natural position is a handicap — Darragh O'Keeffe is a high-quality booking that could help him navigate traffic.|
runners_data.comment: Three pulled-ups in recent starts make Clever Court hard to trust, and a trainer firing at just 4% compounds the concern; he does have experience of today's trip and going, and a win two starts back at least confirms he can cross the line.

runners_data.name: Cruisin Susan
runners_data.note: A 9-year-old hold-up horse (0W2P from good ground) who has placed at 24f, though her broader record is modest; she's being shuffled forward out of her natural position, and at this stage of her career and this level of competition her ability to get competitive is in doubt.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Cruisin Susan does bring distance and going experience to the table, and a third last time out offers a flicker of hope; however, carrying 140 lb and ranked tenth of seventeen, she faces a stiff ask to convert that recent placed effort into something more.

runners_data.name: Fair Damsel
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare for Cian Collins who won at 16f and placed at 20f on good ground (1W2P); the step to 3 miles looks a significant stamina question given her wins have come at shorter trips, and the Reserve 1 jockey booking adds uncertainty.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts, Fair Damsel nonetheless brings distance and going experience to the table, and at a rating of 100 she shapes as a genuine threat at the weights — though 164 lb is a stiff burden to overcome.

runners_data.name: Sineads Fancy
runners_data.note: Prominent-tracking mare (1W3P from good ground, placed at 22f) who maps naturally in the prominent group; a 9-year-old who finished third at 22f in her last good-ground start, and if she gets her natural position off the pace she is entitled to stay involved further than most of this field.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, with a pulled up among her recent efforts, Sineads Fancy faces a stiff task ranked 13 of 17 here; she has run over today's trip and going before, and 17 days off suggests she arrives fresh, but the recent form makes her hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: The Cobblers Wife
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare 86 days off the track with a tongue-tie; her best good-ground result is a 4th at 20f, and the 3-mile trip looks untested — a long layoff plus the out-of-role position map make her one of the hardest to assess with any confidence.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and pulling up most recently, The Cobblers Wife arrives here 86 days fresh and ranked 16 of 17 on our figures — hard to fancy on any angle, though the step back to the track after that break gives connections something to work with.

races.paceDynamic: Tango Theatre and Mobile Mamma are the two confirmed front-runners in a 17-runner field, and both have genuine pace credentials — Tango Theatre won over 26f on good ground and Mobile Mamma is a recent winner who habitually races prominently. With two genuine lead horses pressing each other from the flag over 3 miles on good ground at Wexford, an honest and sustained gallop is the most likely outcome, with neither likely to yield cheaply. That tempo, maintained throughout, will stretch the field and drain the reserves of horses who race too close to it, creating a race that should favour the most resolute stayers who can travel economically in midfield and pick off tired rivals from the home straight. The field holds far more hold-up and prominent types than can all secure their natural positions — Joe's Turn, Set The Tone, Fervida, Strong Contender, Clever Court, Cruisin Susan and The Cobblers Wife are all genuine hold-up horses forced forward on the map, and of the prominent types, Charlie's Dilemma, Clone Cross and Sineads Fancy are the most likely to actually consolidate those berths just behind the pace. The tactical verdict is clear: this race shape strongly favours genuine, efficient hold-up horses with proven stamina at this trip — those who can sit off the strong pace and finish powerfully, led by the likes of Gerrys Wish and Mister Vic.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Pace, Stayers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Tango Theatre and Mobile Mamma set a genuine gallop that stretches the field from halfway, emptying the tanks of those racing prominently.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners trade blows over the final mile, leaving the race wide open for well-held, staying types to surge late down the straight; 3 miles on good ground at this true pace tests stamina above all else, and efficient gallopers who covered ground cheaply will hit the line freshest.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runners Outstay Field
scenarios.trigger: If one or both of the lead horses establish a sustainable rhythm rather than a war early, allowing them to conserve enough to last home over this demanding 3-mile trip.
scenarios.body: Mobile Mamma in particular has shown the ability to dictate and control, and if she gets an uncontested lead or a comfortable target in Tango Theatre she could steal a winning march on the field; the good ground suits both, and a 17-runner field may give them cover to build a cushion in the early stages.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Racers Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely contested but not truly brutal, allowing the prominent-tracking types immediately off the leaders to travel comfortably and pounce before the true hold-up horses get into gear.
scenarios.body: Charlie's Dilemma, Clone Cross and Sineads Fancy are all capable of racing just off the pace and have the good-ground form to sustain their efforts over this trip; in a race where the front two don't fully empty each other, these horses can poach the positions that matter entering the straight.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Overwhelm Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is fierce enough to destroy nearly every horse in the first circuit, leaving a handful of true hold-up specialists to sweep through the wreckage in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: This is the least likely shape given that many of the true hold-up horses are running out of role, displaced forward on the map, making a clean late swoop hard to execute; only Gerrys Wish and possibly Clever Court have the genuine hold-up profile and stamina to capitalise if the race truly falls apart.

watchPoints.text: Mobile Mamma and Tango Theatre will lock horns from the flag — watch whether either capitulates on the first circuit or whether they press each other into a genuinely punishing gallop that shapes the entire race.|

Gerrys Wish arrives just 15 days after his last run having finished second here at this course — watch Jack Kennedy's positioning in the first mile, as the horse's good-ground placed record suggests he peaks in races exactly like this.|

Several hold-up horses including Joe's Turn, Set The Tone and Clever Court are being squeezed out of their natural positions by the volume of hold-up types in the field — watch in the early stages whether any of them fight for position forward or accept a berth and lose their running style.|

Clone Cross has a form string containing falls and pullings-up alongside his placed efforts — watch his jumping closely in the early part of the race, as a 5-year-old over 3 miles with a patchy jumping record is a risk in a large field.|

The Reserve jockeys on Fair Damsel, Sineads Fancy and The Cobblers Wife are a downgrade risk in a 17-runner handicap hurdle where positioning in the early stages is critical — watch how quickly those mounts settle into their places.|

races.name: Pat Farrell Memorial Handicap Hurdle (Div I)

runners_data.name: Jonny Carrol
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the race; Miss Ella Herbison's 7lb claim eases the weight burden, and 15 days between runs is a sharp enough turnaround for a 5yo — will bowl along alone and how long he lasts into the straight is the central question of the race.
runners_data.comment: Placed third four starts back, Jonny Carrol has struggled since but returns fit on 15 days' rest, has run over today's trip and going, and our rating of 109 marks him as the one to beat in this field of 17, even if winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Deise Crystal
runners_data.note: Placed twice at 17f on Good ground in recent form, suggesting she handles conditions well; Anna McGuinness claims 7lb, and the 72-day break could mean she comes here fresh — her hold-up style may see her racing closer than usual given midfield congestion.
runners_data.comment: Deise Crystal posted back-to-back minor finishes — third last time out and a second two starts back — and has experience of today's going, giving him strong claims off a 96 official mark; the 72-day absence and 164 lb burden are the chief concerns.

runners_data.name: Layenda
runners_data.note: Finished third at 19f on Good ground last time but carries a fades-in-finish flag that is a real concern at this stamina-testing 2m4f trip; Ross Berry's 7lb claim is an asset but the form pattern suggests she'll do her best work before the final obstacles.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts — including a pulled up and a ninth — Layenda does bring going experience to the table and ran third two starts back, but 54 days off the track and a hefty 163 lb burden make her prospects here look limited.

runners_data.name: Bayonetta
runners_data.note: Arguably the most consistent horse in the race with seven placed efforts from 15 starts on Good-equivalent ground; Keith Donoghue is a strong booking at this level and her hold-up/midfield style suits a controlled tempo where she can produce late momentum.
runners_data.comment: Consistent placed efforts in recent starts, Bayonetta has back-to-back seconds in her recent form and has run over today's trip and going before — her rating of 100 makes her a leading threat among 17 rivals; the concern is she remains winless in her last five.

runners_data.name: Riverstown Boy
runners_data.note: Five consecutive fifth-place finishes suggest reliable but uninspired form; as the only other prominent-style runner he is likely to track Jonny Carrol closely, and a step up to 2m4f from shorter trips marks the key unknown.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and yet to trouble the judge, Riverstown Boy at least returns on a going surface he has encountered before and is fresh enough after 28 days off; carrying 162 lb against a competitive field of 17 will test his ability to improve on that persistent fifth-place pattern.

runners_data.name: Barrogstown Girl
runners_data.note: Won two of her last 15 starts on Good ground and is on a 14-day turnaround for trainer Jarlath Fahey who has a healthy 1/7 strike rate this fortnight; Peter Smithers claims 7lb and she has shown she can place from off the pace at this course configuration.
runners_data.comment: Placed last time out but winless in her last four starts overall, Barrogstown Girl has run over today's going before and returns on a quick 14-day turnaround; the 157 lb burden could be the factor that keeps her from threatening at the finish.

runners_data.name: Charlie's Gift
runners_data.note: Tumbling form figures ending in F and P hint at jumping fragility or motivation issues; the 53-day break for trainer John Burke and 2m4f trip on Good ground at least match his historical distances, but there is little in the form to suggest he resolves his inconsistency here.
runners_data.comment: Yet to score in his last five starts, with two successive mishaps — a fall then a pulled up — clouding his recent picture; Charlie's Gift has run over today's trip and going, but 157 lb is a stern ask for a gelding whose form is hard to read right now.

runners_data.name: Zaryagle
runners_data.note: A 292-day absence is an enormous fitness query for any jumper; OR 86 looks fair but the trainer's 0/18 T14 record underlines the stable's quiet run, and while this horse has genuine hold-up tendencies it is mapped to midfield given the crowded rear — that compression may actually suit a long-absent horse finding its feet.
runners_data.comment: Rated 104 and ranked second of 17 runners, Zaryagle has run over today's going and is well treated on official ratings — the main concern is his pulling-up last time out after 292 days off, leaving fitness a genuine question mark.

runners_data.name: Madam Elle
runners_data.note: All five historical runs have come on Yielding-to-Heavy going on the Flat and any exposure here is a significant step into the unknown on Good turf; the fades-in-finish flag compounds the concern, and a 156-day absence means fitness cannot be assumed — a natural hold-up type now squeezed into midfield.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and absent for 156 days, Madam Elle faces a stiff ask carrying 153 lb, and our rating of 77 ranks her 14th of 17 here — hard to fancy on these figures, though she does have a seventh-place finish to her name.

runners_data.name: Notmiwadi
runners_data.note: Five recent runs at 16-18f on Good ground show consistent mid-to-rear finishes with no win and a fades-in-finish pattern; the trainer has an impressive 0/25 T14 record in terms of volume but no winners, and this horse racing closer than its preferred style makes a win difficult to construct.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, with a string of mid-to-tail-of-field finishes, Notmiwadi is hard to fancy ranked 16 of 17 on our figures; she has run over today's going before, which offers a small crumb of comfort, but the evidence here is against her.

runners_data.name: Itaintmebabe
runners_data.note: Won at 20f on Soft last season and Gordon Elliott's 1/43 T14 suggests the yard is not in peak form; a genuinely held-up horse pressed into midfield by the crowd dynamic, and the 85-day break without an obvious fitness signal tempers expectations.
runners_data.comment: Itaintmebabe landed a win four starts back but has been unplaced or out of the frame in his three subsequent runs, and 85 days off the track adds a fitness query; he has run over today's trip and going, though 152 lb is a stern weight to overcome.

runners_data.name: Who's Da Goose
runners_data.note: A lightly raced 4yo with only three runs, the shortest field experience here; trainer McCarthy has 1/7 T14 which is a minor positive, but form figures of 7-5-8 on similar ground show it has yet to find the winning thread — pushed toward midfield when its heart lies at the back.
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and still open to improvement, Who's Da Goose has been winless in his last three starts but shaped best when fifth of those three; the 28-day break looks a fair freshener, and with only a handful of runs to his name, there is likely more to come at 152lb.

runners_data.name: Sekakarma
runners_data.note: A 9yo who has placed at 18f on Good recently, suggesting the trip holds no fears; Donagh Meyler rides and the horse appears to have been freshened on a 24-day turnaround, but a natural hold-up operator now in a compressed midfield environment with a modest OR of 79.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Sekakarma does at least bring distance and going experience to the table, and 24 days since his fourth last time out suggests he arrives fresh; however, a pulled up four starts back and that 147 lb burden make it hard to fancy him with conviction.

runners_data.name: Hob's Angel
runners_data.note: The 10yo has a win and four places from 13 recent Good-ground runs — the best strike rate from consistent conditions in the field; a hold-up type mapped toward midfield, but Daniel King's experience and the horse's proven ability to stay 2m4f on Good give it genuine each-way claims.
runners_data.comment: Hob's Angel has shown she can compete, with a win and a second in recent starts, but ranked 12 of 17 on our figures she faces a stiff task here, and 145 lb adds further to the burden.

runners_data.name: Keep The Head
runners_data.note: Form figures of P9P-P0 tell a bleak tale, and the fades-in-finish warning aligns with that pattern; a 15-day turnaround for trainer Hanlon (1/17 T14) offers a minor angle but there is nothing in the recent evidence to suggest a revival at this trip.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and having pulled up on three of those occasions, Keep The Head makes for a difficult proposition here; she does return on a quick turnaround with going experience to her name, but ranked 13 of 17 on our figures, she faces a stiff task.

runners_data.name: John Dixen
runners_data.note: A 4yo with form figures of 0-0-0-6-0 on a variety of surfaces, yet to show any sign of breaking into the places; a hold-up horse by inclination operating at OR 74 with Reserve 2 in the saddle — the redistribution to midfield is secondary to the absence of any form peak to anchor confidence.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked 15th of 17 on our figures, John Dixen faces a stiff ask here; a sixth two starts back offers slim encouragement, and at least he arrives fit on a 17-day turnaround.

runners_data.name: Backinabit
runners_data.note: Won at 17f on Good last season and placed at 16-18f recently — the form basis is there; a 1-day break is eye-catching and trainer Hogan has a lively 2/32 T14 record suggesting live horses run from this yard, but the fades-in-finish tag and Reserve 3 jockey booking create enough doubt to temper enthusiasm.
runners_data.comment: Landed a win three starts back but has struggled since, posting an eighth and a ninth in his last two — and at just one day since his previous outing, the turnaround is sharp. Has run over today's trip and going, though his ranking of 11th of 17 suggests he faces stiff competition.

races.paceDynamic: Jonny Carrol is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 17-horse field and, crucially, faces no identified challenger for the lead — he will stride out from the front and set a sustainable, metronomic gallop on Good ground over 2m4f without any rival applying pressure to his flanks. Riverstown Boy is the only other horse with prominent tendencies and is likely to track Jonny Carrol in second or third, but neither horse is likely to inject a scorching pace, meaning the tempo will be honest rather than brutal. The field holds considerably more hold-up horses than the race shape can accommodate at the rear — Who's Da Goose, Zaryagle, Notmiwadi, Itaintmebabe and several others are genuine hold-up types but have been mapped to midfield because the back of the field is oversaturated; most of them will race closer than their natural style through practical necessity. A controlled, single-pace gallop run by Jonny Carrol with no sustained pressure suits horses that can travel prominently and produce a clean jump at the last — the profile that benefits most is the prominent/mid-division horse with a reliable jumping record on Good ground who can quicken over the final two flights, not the pure hold-up horse forced to cover ground from the rear.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Jonny Carrol Controls; Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Jonny Carrol dictates a steady-to-honest tempo and the field strings out, allowing a prominent or mid-division horse to peel off his back and hit the front approaching the last.
scenarios.body: Jonny Carrol sets a comfortable gallop that keeps the field within range but controlled; a horse travelling fluently just off the pace — likely Deise Crystal, Barrogstown Girl or Bayonetta — picks up the pieces when Jonny Carrol's stamina is tested in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Lasts Home
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so sedately managed that Jonny Carrol conserves enough energy to sustain his gallop over the last two hurdles and hold on under Miss Ella Herbison.
scenarios.body: A very modest tempo suits a front-runner who jumps well and is fresh off a 15-day break; the hold-up horses mapped wide in midfield are too far back to close the gap when the race lacks a decisive quickening phase.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Horse Quickens Clear
scenarios.trigger: If a prominent tracker jumps slickly at the second-last and kicks away before hold-up horses can mount a challenge from the congested midfield.
scenarios.body: Riverstown Boy or Barrogstown Girl, both physically close to the pace throughout, exploit a flat-lined tempo by asserting early in the straight; true hold-up horses like Zaryagle and Notmiwadi, already racing out of role in a compressed midfield, find themselves with too much ground to make up.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Springs Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If the tempo is stronger than expected — perhaps Riverstown Boy pushes Jonny Carrol along — and the field comes back to horses with late energy.
scenarios.body: Even in this scenario most of the redistributed hold-up horses (Zaryagle, Notmiwadi, Itaintmebabe) are racing out of their natural position and may lack the clear passage needed to deliver a sustained finish; Bayonetta's consistent placed form on Good ground gives it the best credentials among the deeper runners.

watchPoints.text: Jonny Carrol jumping cleanly at every hurdle is critical — if he pings his obstacles he could steal enough of a margin that no rival from the congested midfield can reel him in before the line.

Hob's Angel has the best consistency record on Good ground in the entire field and Daniel King knows how to hunt down front-runners; watch where he settles in the first half-mile as a position closer than the map suggests would mark him as a serious danger.

Bayonetta has been placed seven times in 15 Good-ground runs and Keith Donoghue rarely wastes big-race bookings at this level — a clean round of jumping and a clear run from midfield could see her produce the kind of sustained late effort that this tempo invites.

The midfield cluster of redistributed hold-up horses (Zaryagle, Notmiwadi, Itaintmebabe, Who's Da Goose) is likely to cause traffic problems jumping the second-last — a horse getting a bump or checked run here could easily cost several lengths in what may be a close finish.

Backinabit's 1-day turnaround combined with a Hogan stable in form (2/32 T14) is unusual enough to note — if the yard is deliberately targeting this race off a tight break, the horse's previous Good-ground win at 17f is a relevant form reference even with the Reserve 3 jockey concern.

races.name: Pat Farrell Memorial Handicap Hurdle (Div II)

runners_data.name: Poppycon
runners_data.note: The confirmed pace-setter here, although this is a prominent rather than pure lead style; ran twice at this trip on Good ground recently with a placed effort, handles conditions and the uncontested lead is a significant advantage, though the STYLE_FIT flag mildly tempers confidence it will dominate from the front.
runners_data.comment: Placed last time out and a second four starts back, Poppycon brings solid placed form to this race and has run over today's trip and going, while our rating of 97 marks him out as a leading contender — though he remains winless in recent starts, and that fall three runs back is a concern.

runners_data.name: Chosen Princess
runners_data.note: 88-day break is a concern for a 5-year-old, but John M Burke does send them ready and the Good ground suits her form profile; sits naturally prominent and is well-placed to track Poppycon and capitalise if the leader weakens late.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts and carrying a hefty 163 lb, Chosen Princess nevertheless has experience over today's trip and going, and her rating of 92 marks her as a leading threat — though a run of 88 days off the track is the key question mark.

runners_data.name: Thurman
runners_data.note: Hold-up style with a 105-day layoff handled by an amateur rider, which adds risk in a 17-runner field; Good ground form is adequate across five runs but has never threatened to win, and the long absence is the key question mark here.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts and pulling up two outings back are clear concerns, though she has run over today's trip and a 105-day break could mean she returns freshened; the 160 lb burden makes improvement hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Ballyminnion Boy
runners_data.note: Trainer McCarthy in decent recent form (1 from 7 in 14 days) but this horse shows a clear pattern of fading in the finish and has posted three consecutive out-of-the-money finishes on identical Good ground — the fade flag makes it hard to recommend as a beneficiary of any scenario.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, including a fall and a pull-up, Ballyminnion Boy arrives here 28 days later carrying 158 lb with a tough ask ahead; experience over today's going offers some hope, but his recent record gives little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Las Brisas Boy
runners_data.note: Placed at 2m4f on Good ground most recently and the trip clearly suits — headgear (tongue strap) is a positive flag; the fade-in-finish tag is a mild worry, but the relevant form is better than handicap mark of 87 suggests and Kieren Buckley is an able rider.
runners_data.comment: Placed last time out and carrying a testing 157 lb, Las Brisas Boy brings distance-and-going experience to this and our rating of 91 marks him out as a serious threat; the concern is he remains winless in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Larkins Lane
runners_data.note: Won twice at 2m4f on Good/Soft this year and the trip is demonstrably the sweet spot; the 8-from-20f record on Good ground is the headline and makes this one of the most shape-appropriate runners in the field for a steadily-run staying test.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 12 of 17 on our figures and carrying a hefty 155 lb, Larinks Lane is hard to fancy despite her two wins in her last five starts — that eighth last time out is the more recent pointer, and a trainer firing at just 4% over the last 14 days adds little confidence, even if she has run over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Davitts Quay
runners_data.note: Consistent record of fading and finishing out of the frame, and crucially a genuine hold-up type pushed into midfield on the map due to the field's high hold-up count — the redistribution means it may not even get its natural position, compounding a poor recent run sequence.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with a pull-up the most recent effort, Davitts Quay faces a stiff task here — ranked 11 of 17 on our figures — though experience on today's going and a run just 15 days ago at least confirm fitness and familiarity with conditions.

runners_data.name: Ballinvasas Best
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old with four consecutive top-six finishes at around 2m4f on Good ground, showing consistent placed form; prominent style gives it a good tactical position without needing the pace to collapse, and Ryan's yard has a quiet book (0/0 in 14 days) so this horse is likely fresh.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Ballinvasas Best has run over today's trip and going before, and 17 days since her last outing suggests she's fit enough — but a mark of 81 and 151 lb to carry make the task harder for this consistent but elusive mare.

runners_data.name: Mother Ship
runners_data.note: Darragh O'Keeffe is a significant jockey booking for a horse that has placed three times in its last five runs on Good/Good-Soft; however, it is a true hold-up type running in midfield by necessity, not choice — that redistribution reduces its ability to produce a clean finishing effort in a big field.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts with a pulled-up effort among them, Mother Ship faces questions about consistency, though she has run over today's trip and going before and our rating of 89 suggests some untapped ability; a trainer firing at just 5% lately is the concern.

runners_data.name: China Grill
runners_data.note: J J Slevin is an elite booking but the formbook is brutally consistent — four finishes of 10th or worse on Good ground, including a run at this trip; the fade flag and the redistribution away from its natural style make it very difficult to identify an angle of attack.
runners_data.comment: Yet to score in his last four starts, China Grill arrives here 32 days on from his latest outing carrying 150 lb, but remains lightly raced and unexposed — there is scope for improvement as connections look to find a way through.

runners_data.name: Drumadeise
runners_data.note: Has finished 11th, 13th, 12th and 15th across all four career hurdle starts, always on Good ground, always fading — a hold-up type forced further forward by the field's makeup is unlikely to reverse this trend, and Dylan Whelan's 7lb claim does not change the underlying form.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts and ranked 15th of 17 on our figures, Drumadeise faces a stiff task here; she has run over today's going before, and 28 days between runs suggests she arrives fresh, but that's about as far as the positives stretch.

runners_data.name: Esticky End
runners_data.note: Won on Good at 2m and placed at 2m1f, and the step to 2m4f is the key unknown; Pat O'Brien's 5lb claim adds appeal and the recent form string (5-7P21) shows a horse bouncing back to form — one of the few redistributed hold-up types with genuinely recent winning form to point to.
runners_data.comment: Pulled up two starts back makes him hard to trust despite a win last time out; he has run over today's going before, but ranked 14th of 17 on our figures and carrying 149 lb, there are significant questions to answer here.

runners_data.name: Ballinaboola Gold
runners_data.note: Twice placed at 2m4f on Good ground and Danny Mullins is a top booking, but the fade flag and redistribution away from a true hold-up position both dampen the appeal; the 15-day turnaround is fine, but the 9th last time out at this trip on identical going is hard to ignore.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, though a second four starts back shows she can threaten — her going experience and a quick 15-day turnaround keep her in the mix, but a rating of 77 and recent regression toward the rear make a big run hard to pin down.

runners_data.name: Dark Berkshire
runners_data.note: Third at 2m3f on Good ground as recently as the last-but-two run shows there is ability here, and P J Rothwell's runners can be found fit on a short turnaround; hold-up by nature and squeezed into midfield by the redistribution, but the form is more respectable than many in this field.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with a pulled-up and two single-figure finishes among them, Dark Berkshire is hard to fancy ranked 13 of 17 on our figures; a trainer in dire form at 1/26 over 14 days compounds the concern, though he does return quickly and has run over today's going before.

runners_data.name: Little Boy Sivola
runners_data.note: No jockey listed which adds uncertainty; hold-up type with a headgear flag (tongue strap/blindfold) and a poor recent run sequence culminating in a pulled-up effort — the redistribution away from the back of the field further limits its tactical options in a big, competitive field.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and pulling up most recently, Little Boy Sivola arrives on a retrieval mission with a struggling yard — just one from 26 in the past fortnight. Has run over today's going, and 147 lb is no help.

runners_data.name: Laligurash
runners_data.note: Four-year-old with a consistent record in the 7th-10th range on Good ground and a fade flag; the redistribution into midfield removes the natural position a hold-up horse needs, and the form line of 10-8-7-12 gives no evidence of imminent improvement.
runners_data.comment: Lightly raced and unexposed, Laligurash has shown little in recent starts — unplaced last time out, with an eighth and seventh before that — yet to score in his last five, but the limited profile leaves plenty of questions unanswered and room to progress.

runners_data.name: General Clermont
runners_data.note: Raced just yesterday (1-day turnaround) which is the dominant factor — either this was an intended quick double entry or an admin quirk, but the physical freshness of a 10-year-old after a race the prior day is a significant concern; has placed six times in career but the recent form shows 14th, 9th, pulled-up and 9th, and the no-jockey flag adds uncertainty.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and pulling up two outings back is a concern, but General Clermont has distance and going experience to call on, and our rating of 108 marks him a cut above this field despite a taxing 168 lb burden.

races.paceDynamic: Poppycon is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 17-runner field and, critically, faces no genuine pace rival to push them along — this sets up a controlled, sustainable gallop on Good ground at Wexford over 2m4f. With Chosen Princess and Ballinvasas Best tracking prominently behind, the early shape should be orderly rather than pressured, allowing Poppycon to dictate a rhythm that suits stayers rather than speedsters. The bulk of this field — Laligurash, Davitts Quay, Mother Ship, China Grill, Drumadeise and several others — are genuine hold-up types that have been redistributed to midfield on the map because there are simply too many closers for all to settle in their natural rear positions, meaning the true back-markers will be bunched and reliant on traffic breaking cleanly late. This race shape — one uncontested leader, a genuine staying pace, Good ground — strongly favours hold-up horses with proven stamina at the trip who can produce a sustained late run rather than a sharp turn of foot, and prominent types who can slot in behind the leader without burning energy will also be well-placed.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Stayers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Poppycon dictates a genuine but unhurried gallop and the prominent group conserves energy through the middle of the race.
scenarios.body: Poppycon's uncontested lead sets a steady pace that brings the field to the final two hurdles in a compact group, rewarding those who travelled smoothly in midfield and can sustain their run; true stayers with distance form on Good ground will finish strongest when the sprint develops.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Duo Steal It
scenarios.trigger: If Chosen Princess or Ballinvasas Best press Poppycon into a rhythm just brisk enough to string out the field before hold-up horses can organise.
scenarios.body: The pace turns genuine enough to compromise closers who need to improve from further back, and a prominent tracker sitting a length or two off the leader simply outstays the field without ever being headed late; the trip at 2m4f on easy ground suits the prominent-style finisher.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Swamp Leader
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is slow enough to produce a sprint finish from the final hurdle, allowing the rear-of-midfield group to close en masse.
scenarios.body: A compressed field means many horses arrive in contention simultaneously at the last, and those with a clean passage and proven recent form — particularly Esticky End and Larkins Lane — can pick off tiring rivals in the run-in; Good ground suits a clean late burst rather than grinding attrition.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos in Big Field
scenarios.trigger: If the 17-runner field creates traffic problems, fallers or interference that disrupts the expected shape entirely.
scenarios.body: With so many hold-up horses stacked in the rear third of the field, any bunching or interference at the final two flights will cause significant disruption, and only those who have secured daylight early — Poppycon, Chosen Princess — will be unaffected; this scenario most flatters the front-end horses who avoid the carnage.

watchPoints.text: General Clermont's 1-day turnaround is the biggest flag in the race — watch for any market moves or withdrawal that clarifies whether this is a genuine runner or an entry anomaly, as running a 10-year-old back-to-back on Good ground represents a serious freshness risk.

With 17 runners in a 2m4f hurdle at Wexford, watch the early stages for crowding and positional clashes — Laligurash, Mother Ship and Davitts Quay are all genuine hold-up types forced into midfield who may be squeezed for room before the first flight.

Larkins Lane holds the strongest staying form at the exact trip but is trained by P J Rothwell who has sent out 18 runners in the last 14 days without a winner — watch whether the market reflects any yard concern or whether the horse trades shorter given its clear form credentials.

Poppycon wears tongue strap and is the lone pace angle, but has a Fell (F) on its recent form card — watch the market for any confidence signal from the Eoin Doyle yard, as a jumping error would completely collapse the race shape and open it up for closers.

Esticky End and Las Brisas Boy both represent recently-active horses (15 and 26 days respectively) with visible form lines at similar trips — watch these two in the pre-race market as they are among the few redistributed types whose actual form justifies confidence if they find a clear run.
